prompt: Solve the AppWorld task using Python in the persistent execution environment. The variable apis is already available: use it directly. Do not import apps or create another API client. You may reason inside a closed <think>...</think> block before returning exactly one fenced python code block. Do not include prose outside those blocks. Tool observations contain stdout only: a bare API call or assignment does NOT display its return value. Always print query results, including documentation, so you can read them next turn. For example: print(apis.api_docs.show_app_descriptions()). When storing a result, use result = apis.some_app.some_api(...), then print(result). Discover APIs with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_descriptions(app_name=...)) and inspect signatures with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_doc(app_name=..., api_name=...)) before calling them. A documentation query must be the only API call in that response. Print its result, immediately end the code block, and wait for the observation before choosing any further call. Only call task APIs whose exact names and arguments you have already read in observations. Never combine discovery with a guessed API call: an exception discards all earlier stdout from the block. Do not invent API names or arguments. Read each tool observation, and correct the cause when execution fails instead of repeating the same code. Variables persist between executions. Tool observations appear in <tool_response> tags. Use the supervisor completion API only after you have finished the requested task. Authentication: login does not establish an implicit session for later API calls. Read the app's login signature, obtain that app's password from the supervisor, and use the documented username field (often the supervisor's email). A password is not an access token. Save the login response and its access_token in persistent variables. Pass that returned token explicitly to every endpoint whose documented signature requires access_token, including later turns. Do not pass it to endpoints that do not accept it. Never invent token setters or client sessions. Task coverage: before acting, identify the requested entities, data source, filters, date range, and all required outputs. Use the user's own collections when requested; a global search is not a substitute. For all-items requests or totals, inspect pagination arguments and traverse every relevant page until the documented end condition. A default first page is not complete coverage. Before completing, check each requirement against observed results, including recipient identities and relationship filters. Response inspection: API results are already Python objects unless the documentation or observed type says otherwise. After a type or structure error, make a short inspection action that prints type(result), dictionary keys, or a small sample before changing the larger script. Do not call json.loads on an existing list or dictionary. Correct one assumption at a time; do not alternate speculative rewrites.
